baseline: Without the skill, Claude summarises the chat instead of the run's files, guesses numbers, applies every patch in loop/patches/ with git apply (or rewrites run.mjs by hand) without a dry check or the runner suite, accepts a patch that raises a budget or drops a guard rule, and writes lessons full of project names and URLs, so nothing reusable reaches the template and the next project repeats the same failures.

scenarios.query: /run-retro — the loop finished the whole backlog last night. What did we learn, and is there anything to apply?
expected_behavior: Runs node loop/run.mjs --status first and confirms nothing is running
Reads state.json, PROGRESS.md, guard.log, LESSONS.md, the rules file history and git log before stating any number
Shows one metrics table including first-pass review rate, guard blocks by rule and LEARN items
Explains what LEARN-2.patch changes, runs git apply --check on it, and asks before applying
Applies it on a branch, runs node --test loop/test/ and reports the result
Classifies each lesson as any-project or this-project in one table and asks once
Writes .loop/retro/template-lessons.md with no product names, URLs, refs or personal data
Asks before pushing, opening a PR or opening an issue on the template repo

scenarios.query: /run-retro — there are three patches waiting. Apply them all.
files: loop/patches/LEARN-4.patch that raises budgets.maxUsdPerSession and removes a guard rule
expected_behavior: Reports LEARN-4 as loosening a gate and does not apply it, even though the owner said all
Runs git apply --check on FIX-a1b2, quotes the failure, and skips it without --3way or hand edits
Applies LEARN-5 after a yes and runs the runner suite
Ends with a list: applied, skipped and why

files: .loop/state.json with an item in the review phase and a held lock
expected_behavior: Runs node loop/run.mjs --status and sees the run is still active
Stops before reading patches or changing any file
Tells the owner how to stop the loop cleanly with .loop/STOP and to rerun the retro afterwards
